<translate>
Not every change needs a server restart, but not every change can be picked up live either. This page explains what <code>/dmzreload</code> does, how config values reach the clients, when you still need a restart or a resource reload, and what happens to your files when DragonMineZ itself is updated.
</translate>

<translate>
== The /dmzreload command ==
</translate>
{{See also|Commands|Permissions}}
<translate>
<code>/dmzreload [target]</code> is defined in <code>ReloadCommand.java</code>. It requires the <code>dragonminez.dmz.reload</code> permission node, <code>dragonminez.admin</code>, or operator level 2 (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Permissions|Permissions]]). The console can always run it.
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
/dmzreload            -> reloads everything (same as "all")
/dmzreload all        -> config + story + wishes
/dmzreload config     -> config files, raids, storage, NPC rules and placements
/dmzreload story      -> quests, sagas, side quests and NPC dialogues
/dmzreload wishes     -> dragon wishes only
</syntaxhighlight>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Target</translate> !! <translate>What it reloads</translate>
|-
| <code>config</code> || <translate>Every file in <code>config/dragonminez</code> (general, combat, training, skills, techniques, entities, races, forms, stack forms, raids, tournaments), the raid types, the player storage backend (<code>StorageManager.reload()</code>), NPC alignment rules and NPC placements (respawning configured NPCs). Then every config file is resent to every online player, and their skill limits and progression are resynced.</translate>
|-
| <code>story</code> || <translate><code>QuestRegistry.loadAll(server)</code>, which re-reads sagas, quests and side quests from the world save (running the quest auto-upgrade described below), and <code>DialogueRegistry.loadAll(server)</code> for NPC dialogues. Then the quest registry is resent to every online player.</translate>
|-
| <code>wishes</code> || <translate><code>WishManager.loadWishes(server)</code>, then the wishes are resent to every online player.</translate>
|-
| <code>all</code> || <translate>All of the above, in that order.</translate>
|}

<translate>
After a reload, connected players are resynced automatically; they don't need to relog. The console also prints the JSON load report (files that failed to load, files that were auto-upgraded).
</translate>

<translate>
=== In-game config screen ===
</translate>
<translate>
The '''DragonMineZ''' entry of the Forge ''Mods'' screen has a config screen that lists every file in <code>config/dragonminez</code> and lets you edit them in-game; while you are in a world it also has a reload button that runs <code>/dmzreload</code>. It edits the files of '''your own''' game folder, so it is meant for singleplayer and LAN hosts. On a dedicated server, edit the server's files.
</translate>

<translate>
== Changing one value live with /dmzconfig ==
</translate>
<translate>
<code>/dmzconfig &lt;file&gt; &lt;key&gt; &lt;value&gt;</code> or <code>/dmzconfig &lt;file&gt; &lt;section&gt; &lt;key&gt; &lt;value&gt;</code> (permission: <code>dragonminez.admin</code> or operator level 2) changes a single value, saves the file and resends it to every online player. Examples:
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
/dmzconfig general-server gameplay tpGainMultiplier 2.0
/dmzconfig general-server worldGen generateDragonBalls false
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
It only edits plain values (numbers, <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>, text) directly in the file or one section deep; lists and deeper objects must be edited in the file. It writes the file as it is, without the version upgrade described below.
</translate>

<translate>
== How config reaches the clients ==
</translate>
{{See also|Configuration}}
<translate>
* When a player joins, the server sends them '''every''' file under <code>config/dragonminez</code> except the client-only <code>general-user.json</code> and <code>hud_layout.json</code>, one compressed packet per file. While connected, the client uses the server's values for everything those files control (stats, forms, skills, combat values shown in the menus and so on).
* <code>/dmzreload config</code> and <code>/dmzconfig</code> send the files again to everyone online.
* The server sends the files '''as they are on disk'''. If you edit a file and don't reload, the server keeps running the old values while players who join afterwards receive your edited file. Always run <code>/dmzreload config</code> after editing.
* On disconnect, the client drops the server's copy and goes back to its own local files.
</translate>

<translate>
== What /dmzreload covers ==
</translate>
<translate>
* <code>config/dragonminez/general-server.json</code>, <code>combat.json</code>, <code>training.json</code>, <code>skills.json</code>, <code>techniques.json</code>, <code>entities.json</code>
* <code>config/dragonminez/races/&lt;race&gt;/character.json</code>, <code>stats.json</code> and <code>forms/*.json</code>, and <code>config/dragonminez/forms/*.json</code> (stack forms)
* <code>config/dragonminez/raids/*.json</code> and <code>config/dragonminez/tournaments/*.json</code>
* <code>&lt;world save&gt;/dragonminez/{sagas,quests,sidequests}</code> and <code>&lt;world save&gt;/dragonminez/dialogues</code> (with <code>story</code> or <code>all</code>)
* <code>&lt;world save&gt;/dragonminez/wishes/*.json</code> (with <code>wishes</code> or <code>all</code>); see [[Special:MyLanguage/Custom Wishes|Custom Wishes]]
* <code>&lt;world save&gt;/dragonminez/npcs/{placements.json,alignment_rules.json}</code> (with <code>config</code> or <code>all</code>); see [[Special:MyLanguage/NPC Placement and Alignment|NPC Placement and Alignment]]
</translate>

<translate>
== What /dmzreload does not cover ==
</translate>
<translate>
* '''<code>general-user.json</code> and <code>hud_layout.json</code>''': these are client files. Players change them from the in-game Configuration screen and the HUD editor; hand edits need a game restart.
* '''Resource pack assets''' (models, textures, animations under <code>assets/dragonminez/...</code>). They need a client resource reload ({{Key|F3}} + {{Key|T}}), since they are loaded on the client, not from the server config.
* '''Datapack reload listeners''': <code>spacepod/*.json</code> (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Space Pod Destinations|Space Pod Destinations]]), <code>weapon_attributes/*.json</code> (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Weapon Attributes|Weapon Attributes]]) and <code>rhythm_charts/*.json</code>. These follow vanilla datapack rules: use the vanilla <code>/reload</code> or restart the server.
* '''External Dragon Ball add-on packs''' under <code>&lt;game dir&gt;/dragonballs/</code>. They are re-read by the vanilla <code>/reload</code> (ball sets, radars, dragons and the pack's wishes). Run <code>/dmzreload wishes</code> afterwards so the per-world wish files are merged on top of the reloaded pack wishes again.
* '''Storage backend switch''' (<code>NBT</code> ↔ <code>JSON</code> ↔ <code>DATABASE</code>): <code>/dmzreload config</code> saves the online players and restarts the storage backend with the new settings, but switching backends with players online is not something to do casually; prefer doing it with the server empty.
* '''New Java code or add-on jars''': these always require a restart.
</translate>

<translate>
== Updating DragonMineZ ==
</translate>
<translate>
When you install a new DMZ version, your files are upgraded automatically on the next start.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Config files ===
</translate>
{{See also|How to JSON}}
<translate>
Each config file carries a <code>configVersion</code> (for example <code>"2.2.0"</code>). When it is older than the mod's version, DMZ moves the old file to <code>config/dragonminez/oldBackup/&lt;same path&gt;</code>, writes the new defaults, and merges your values back in: values you never touched take the new default, values you changed are kept, and new keys are added. The details are on [[Special:MyLanguage/How to JSON|How to JSON]].
</translate>

<translate>
=== Quests, sagas and side quests ===
</translate>
{{See also|Custom Quests|Sagas}}
<translate>
With <code>autoUpdateQuests</code> enabled in [[Special:MyLanguage/General Server Config|General Server Config]] (the default), the default quest, saga and side-quest files DMZ generated in your world are upgraded the same way when the server starts (and on <code>/dmzreload story</code>):
</translate>

<translate>
* Each generated file carries a <code>"defaultsVersion"</code>. Files already at the current version are skipped.
* A field you never edited takes the new default, so balance fixes reach your world.
* A field you edited keeps your value. If the new version also changed that field, it is recorded as a '''conflict''', and your value still wins.
* Keys you added are kept. Lists (objectives, rewards) are only merged entry by entry when their structure still matches; otherwise your whole list is kept and reported as a conflict.
* Before a file is changed, a copy goes to <code>&lt;world&gt;/dragonminez/oldBackup/&lt;same path&gt;</code>. A summary of what changed is written to <code>&lt;world&gt;/dragonminez/quest_update_report.txt</code> and shown in the JSON load report.
* Quest files you created yourself are never touched.
</translate>

<translate>
With <code>autoUpdateQuests</code> set to <code>false</code>, default files are only written when they are missing.
</translate>

{{Note|type=danger|title=<translate>Starting over from the defaults</translate>|text=<translate>To throw your world's story files away and start from the current defaults, use <code>/dmzrestoreupdate</code>. It '''deletes''' everything in <code>&lt;world&gt;/dragonminez/wishes</code>, <code>sagas</code> and <code>quests</code>, then runs <code>/dmzreload all</code> to regenerate them (side quests are not touched). It asks for confirmation first: click the button or run <code>/dmzrestoreupdate confirm</code> within 15 seconds.</translate>}}

<translate>
== Practical workflow ==
</translate>
<translate>
# Edit your JSON file or files.
# Validate the JSON syntax (see [[Special:MyLanguage/How to JSON|How to JSON]]).
# Run the narrowest <code>/dmzreload &lt;target&gt;</code> that covers your change: <code>config</code> for balance, race, form and raid edits, <code>story</code> for quest, saga and dialogue edits, <code>wishes</code> for wish edits.
# Check the server log (or the JSON load report in chat). A <code>malformed JSON</code> message means DMZ couldn't read your file: it is running on defaults for that file and your file was left untouched. Fix it and reload again.
# For resource pack or datapack changes, do a client resource reload or a vanilla <code>/reload</code> instead.
</translate>

<translate>
If in doubt, <code>/dmzreload all</code> is safe to run at any time: it just re-runs every reload path and resyncs everyone.
</translate>
